title: Part (b): no matching relative-error lower bound (incoherent case and ε-exponent)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Severity: requirement unmet.** The problem (parts a/b) explicitly asks for *matching lower bounds*. Thm. `thm:fail` proves failure with probability only
$$c=\tfrac{9}{16}\bigl(1+\rho^\star/q\bigr)^{-1},$$
which is a **constant only when $\rho^\star=\Omega(q)$** (partially coherent heaviest column). The authors themselves note that for the **incoherent flat-column** regime $\rho^\star\asymp 1/m$, $c\asymp s/n\to 0$, so *no constant-probability failure is established there*, and the conclusion degrades to $\mathbb E\|\cdot\|\ge(1+c\varepsilon)\tau_k$ with $c\to0$ — essentially no separation.

Hence the lower bound matches the Achlioptas–McSherry / Drineas–Zouzias upper bound **neither**:
- in the $\varepsilon$-exponent ($\varepsilon^{-1}$ lower vs. $\varepsilon^{-2}$ upper — acknowledged in Rem. `rem:cure`), **nor**
- in covering the incoherent regime at all.

The single-column Paley–Zygmund certificate (eq. `eq:EX2`, `eq:failprob`) is fundamentally insufficient for these regimes.

**Suggested fix (hard).** Prove a Davis–Kahan / Wedin $\sin\Theta$ subspace lower bound: for a rank-$k$-plus-flat-incoherent-tail $A$, show uniform sampling at $s=o(\mathrm{sr}(A)\max(m,n)/\varepsilon^2)$ forces a constant angle between the sampled and true top-$k$ subspaces, hence relative error $\ge 1+\Omega(\varepsilon)$ with constant probability. This is the genuine matching converse the problem requests.
